title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations (estimand: verifier‑consistency under identical inputs)
abstract: Estimand and problem statement: this preregistered study tests a narrow estimand—verifier‑consistency under identical generator outputs—asking whether a deterministic validator will treat identical canonical candidates differently across two scoring conditions. Method and design: preregistered paired design (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). We synthesized N = 120 intent→configuration tasks from deterministic templates, generated one canonical LLM candidate per task (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...), and scored each candidate with a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Key quantitative result (confirmatory, preregistered estimator): baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, shared canonical candidate) = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Major limitation and interpretation: because the preregistered confirmatory semantics reused an identical canonical candidate per pair (shared_initial_candidate), the paired result correctly measures validator determinism given identical inputs but does not estimate independent LLM generative reliability under stochastic sampling. We publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑episode traces) and the immutable initial master prompt reference provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration is a core NetOps task where semantic correctness is safety‑critical: incorrect sequences can break reachability, violate ACLs, or create unsafe transient states during multi‑step changes. Deterministic offline validators (reachability/ACL/routing analyzers in the Batfish family and successors) provide auditable oracles for pre‑deployment checks [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Generative LLM pipelines promise rapid intent→config production, but operational adoption requires reliable, auditable measures of correctness. After an autonomous literature review we preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment whose estimand is explicit: verifier‑consistency under identical inputs (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). The manuscript (1) reports the preregistered execution and exact confirmatory statistics grounded in archived artifacts, (2) diagnoses—using archived traces—why the confirmatory paired contrast is degenerate, and (3) provides artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications that preserve reproducibility while answering the more operational question of independent LLM reliability.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluations. Offline semantic validators and configuration analyzers are established tools for pre‑deployment validation and have scalable implementations suitable for realistic topologies (Batfish lineage and related control‑plane verifiers) [doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Prior LLM→NetOps studies vary on sampling semantics (single canonical candidate vs. independent per‑condition sampling), repair‑loop budget, and validator scope. Studies that measure independent generative reliability typically draw independent seeds per condition or employ multi‑seed replication, whereas studies focusing on validator behavior may intentionally reuse identical candidates. Generate–validate–repair is the dominant architectural pattern for operational net automation; our contribution situates a preregistered, artifact‑anchored point in that methodological space and makes explicit which estimand was tested and why.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 before any model calls (preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea...). The preregistration specified: paired design with N = 120 tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, confirmatory generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical LLM candidate per task reused across both scoring episodes), validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, and analysis = paired_binary_analysis_v1 (bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). All artifacts required to reproduce the run are archived and SHA‑256 fingerprinted in execution/execution_manifest.json.

Task synthesis and validator semantics. Tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates (generator_id deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit required_sequence, workflow_policies (for example must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty metadata. The validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performs normalized parsing, enforces workflow_policies (transient and final), computes final_state reachability and ACL invariants, and emits an auditable per‑episode JSON trace archived under execution/scoring/*.json (representative: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...).

Model orchestration and exact model‑call accounting (reviewer request addressed). Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...) records the declared model and invocation parameters. Confirmatory accounting rule (preregistered and executed): a single canonical generation was produced per task and reused for both scoring conditions; model_calls_used = 120 because one shared_initial generation was produced per task (execution/provider_calls/* contains provider call traces for each shared_initial generation). This accounting is explicit in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and in the artifact index we publish. The counting rule is: each generation call is counted once; the reuse of the same canonical candidate across two scoring episodes does not increase model_calls_used in the confirmatory accounting. This is the precise behavior that produced the degenerate paired contingency (n_11 = 120).

Confirmatory analysis plan (frozen). For each task i we recorded baseline_i (binary verifier pass for the deterministic template baseline) and guarded_i (binary verifier pass for the shared canonical LLM candidate). Primary estimator = mean(guarded_i − baseline_i) over i = 1..120. Inference: 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test on the 2×2 contingency. Contamination heuristics (preregistered) used exact‑match and normalized n‑gram overlap thresholds and are archived under analysis/contamination_summary.csv. The complete code, seeds, and per‑episode traces are published so that reruns with alternate generation semantics are deterministic and auditable.
sections.results:
Execution and confirmatory counts (artifact‑anchored). Planned_episode_count = 240 (120 tasks × 2 scoring conditions). Completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial generation per task). Confirmatory outcome: baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count = 120/120. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c7eeaaf...). Primary estimate = 0.00; bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 replicates, seed 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All per‑episode scoring JSON traces support these counts (examples archived: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 8b92a69e..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 0d56c1ad...).

Artifact diagnosis of the degenerate contingency. The recorded artifact chain shows two preregistered, archived design choices that deterministically produced identical validator outcomes per pair: (A) generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one canonical LLM output per task stored at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; representative SHA‑256s: task‑000001 8f38c8be..., task‑000002 ae967f70..., task‑000003 f7f4db24...), and (B) template‑tight tasks encoding explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies that canonical template‑aligned candidates satisfy. Because the validator is deterministic, identical inputs necessarily generate identical pass/fail results across conditions. The per‑episode validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json) show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration, transient checks, and validation_after.valid = true for the canonical candidates; those exact traces are published and fingerprinted, enabling byte‑for‑byte audit of the causal chain.

Confirmatory inference is therefore correct for the preregistered estimand but uninformative about independent LLM sampling reliability. The artifacts permit immediate deterministic reruns with alternative sampling semantics (see Runnable modifications below).
sections.discussion:
What the confirmatory result does and does not show. It correctly answers the preregistered estimand: whether a deterministic validator yields different pass/fail outcomes when fed identical canonical candidates under two scoring conditions (it does not). It does not, and by design cannot, estimate the operational probability that independently sampled LLM outputs will pass a validator; answering that requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed designs. This methodological distinction is central and is made explicit here to prevent overinterpretation.

Runnable, artifact‑grounded next steps (published and deterministic). Using the archived pipeline and fingerprints one can deterministically rerun informative experiments without changing the task set: (1) independent_per_condition confirmatory rerun—generate distinct seeds per condition per task (baseline seed_0, guarded seed_1), rescore with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and recompute paired contrasts; (2) multi‑seed confirmatory design—draw K ≥ 3 independent seeds per condition per task and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (3) validator diversification—score candidates with a second independent verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All inputs required to perform these reruns are archived (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/responses/*) so reruns are deterministic and auditable. These modifications were preregistered as plausible exploratory or follow‑up actions but were not executed in the reported confirmatory run; they are presented here as artifact‑grounded, immediately runnable protocols for researchers and operators.

Threats to validity (artifact‑identified). Internal validity: the shared_initial design intentionally removed generation variance and therefore precluded testing independent generative reliability. Construct validity: template‑aligned tasks and a single deterministic validator increase the chance that canonical candidates pass; they reduce generalizability to open‑language intents. External validity: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the exact recorded invocation and to the deterministic_netops_validator_v5; generalization across models, open prompts, or production topologies is not supported by these artifacts. Contamination: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics flagged no confirmatory items, but such heuristics are imperfect proxies for pretraining exposure. We publish provider call traces and candidate hashes so external contamination analyses can be run without altering archived evidence.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment and published exhaustive per‑episode provider traces, validator JSON traces, and SHA‑256 fingerprints to permit byte‑for‑byte reproduction. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on all N = 120 tasks (both 120/120). Archived artifacts demonstrate that identical canonical candidates and template‑tight task encodings caused the degenerate paired contingency; thus the confirmatory result correctly documents validator determinism but does not address independent LLM sampling reliability. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed replication, validator diversity) to answer independent generative reliability while preserving reproducibility. All execution and analysis artifacts—including the immutable initial master prompt reference provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and the preregistration SHA‑256—are included in the submission bundle to permit exact audit and follow‑up experiments.

Preregistration: CAND-2026-001-NetConfig-Semantic-v1 (frozen prior to execution); preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37. Topic constraints and human role: the Research Director chose the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the autonomous pipeline performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, execution, deterministic validation, analysis, autonomous peer review, and manuscript drafting and revision without human manual editing of technical content. Model‑call accounting: the preregistered confirmatory semantics generated one canonical candidate per task and reused that identical shared_initial candidate for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes; therefore model_calls_used = 120 in the confirmatory accounting (provider call traces archived at execution/provider_calls/* and canonical candidates at execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt). Preregistered confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired_binary_analysis_v1), with confirmatory generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate'; this estimand tests validator consistency under identical inputs and is not an estimator of independent LLM sampling reliability. Execution artifacts and reproducibility: the complete execution manifest, per‑episode provider traces, per‑episode validator JSON traces, seeds, and analysis outputs are published in the artifact bundle; the full manifest path is execution/execution_manifest.json (see that file for per‑file SHA‑256 fingerprints). Contamination detection: preregistered string‑overlap heuristics were run and recorded (analysis/contamination_summary.csv) but string overlap is an imperfect proxy for pretraining exposure; provider call traces and candidate hashes are published to enable external contamination audits. Retries and failures: planned_episode_count = 240, completed_episode_count = 240, failed_episode_count = 0; preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automatic retries for infrastructure failures; none were required. Autonomous boundary and pre‑lock development: the Research Director and AI performed pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal; per the autonomy policy, those pre‑lock artifacts were not used as final empirical evidence. The current manuscript and all reported experimental outcomes derive from post‑lock autonomous execution; every principal file and hash required to reproduce the run is included in the bundle.
limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and limit external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not executed in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
